about: Hand-authored contract for re-reading stored choices (choice_reread.py and ChoiceReread.swift): a small run whose records stored choices read by an older parser, the readings the current parser gives them, the counts a check or a re-read analysis reports, and the effect rows each engine's analyze writes with and without --reread-choices. Every expected value was written by hand from the parsing rules and the paired-difference definition, never read back from either engine. Lines count the non-blank lines of generations.jsonl from 1. Records without finishReason come from an engine older than that field and are read as complete replies.
parserVersionNote: parsingFixtureSHA256 is the SHA-256 of choice-parsing.json when parserVersion was set. When the parsing fixture changes, the parsing rules have changed: bump CHOICE_PARSER_VERSION (judicial.py) and Judicial.choiceParserVersion together, then record the new version and hash here.

records.output: As a doctor, I would choose B.

As a matter of reading, B.

edgeCases.about: Malformed records both engines must read alike, given as exact generations.jsonl lines, re-read against q1's options [A, B]. Line 1: a null condition is the condition "", a null finishReason counts as no finishReason, and a sampleIndex written as 0.0 is not an integer so it is left out of the example. Line 2: a stored value that is not a string names no option, so it is no answer, and a finishReason that is not a string is recorded but is not a cut-off. Line 3: lengthInReasoning is a cut-off.

why.3: unchanged: an option opening the reply, followed by punctuation
why.4: unchanged: the first capital letter standing alone
why.5: unchanged: a valid JSON answer naming A
why.6: unchanged, from an older engine (no finishReason): 'answer is' marker
why.8: changed to another option, the article case: the old parser read the article 'a' as option A
why.9: changed to another option, malformed JSON: unescaped quotes inside the reasons; the answer key is read from the text
why.10: changed to no answer: cut off by the length limit mid-deliberation, which the old parser read as its first-enumerated option
why.11: gained an answer: cut off after a complete answer key, which the old parser could not read
why.13: changed to another option, from an older engine (no finishReason): the article 'a' again, read as a complete reply
why.7 and 14: no answer options, so no parsedChoice: not counted

expected.note: Every record that carries parsedChoice was read again from its stored reply with the choice parser this engine has now. The re-read choices replace the stored ones in this analysis only: every choice outcome, exclusion, and table here uses them. The run directory, including generations.jsonl, was not changed. Records without finishReason come from engines that did not record whether a reply was cut off by the length limit; they were read as complete replies.
expected.sentence: Choices were re-read from the stored replies with choice parser version 2026-10-17; 5 of 12 stored choices changed, and the run itself is unchanged. 2 of those replies come from an older engine that did not record whether a reply was cut off by the length limit, so they were read as complete replies (1 of them changed).

choiceRate.about: The pooled choiceRate row for condition 'steered' against 'baseline': per item, the share of readable replies naming the target B, minus the baseline's; the estimate is the mean of those differences over the items both conditions read. Baseline per item: q1 1, q2 1, q3 1, q4 1, q5 0, q6 1.

stored.workedOut: steered stored: q1 0, q2 0, q3 0, q4 unreadable, q5 1, q6 0; differences q1 -1, q2 -1, q3 -1, q5 +1, q6 -1; mean -3/5
